equity.level_reason: Coverage is reported by county SVI tertile and the gradient is interpreted ('disproportionately affect nursing homes with limited resources'), but SVI groups are only set side by side with CIs; no difference or ratio is computed, so the level is capped at 2.

level_alternative.reason: SVI is an area index used as a stratifier and the gradient is framed and interpreted; if side-by-side tertile values count as quantified, cost and Medicare Part D billing barriers are named as structural explanations.

determinants_of_health.v: barriers related to cost and billing (higher vaccine cost; Medicare Part D billing systems); nursing homes with limited resources

ev.q: suggesting that barriers related to cost and billing disproportionately affect nursing homes with limited resources.
RSV vaccines are billable to Medicare Part D, and some nursing homes do not have systems in place for Part D billing.

equity.equity_measurement: SVI is the county-level tertile of the facility's location, an area proxy for residents' social position; 30 facilities in counties without an SVI score are excluded. Coverage is not disaggregated by resident age, race or individual SES.

notes: CI non-overlap is the stated significance rule, so inference is CIs only. Comparisons with 2023 NHSN coverage and NIS adult coverage are context in the Discussion, not the main analysis. Facility clustering is not addressed in the Poisson models.
